syllabus.clause: transaction, periodic snapshot, accumulating snapshot and factless facts (event and coverage)
how each absorbs late updates and which measures stay additive

at.step: Predict: which types stay additive under a late update?

items.item: A row corresponds to a measurement event at a point in space and time
Transaction fact tables may be dense or sparse; rows exist only if measurements take place
A row summarizes many measurement events over a standard period; the grain is the period, not the transaction

at.step: Predict: does an idle account still get a snapshot row?

items.item: These tables are uniformly dense: a row is inserted for every entity, every period, even with zero activity
A row summarizes events at predictable steps between a process's defined start and end
A row is inserted once, at creation, then revisited and updated as pipeline progress occurs — unique among the fact table types

at.step: Predict: how many rows after three milestones?

items.item: Accumulating snapshots often include numeric lag measurements and milestone completion counters
A measurement event can record only dimension keys coming together, with no numeric fact at all
Subtracting a real activity table from a real coverage table finds the set of events that did not happen
